people.name: Mary Bradley
people.title: Managing Partner
people.persona: Runs the firm the way she reviews a claim set: every word has to earn its place, and nothing goes to a client without her knowing who owns the next deadline. Her engagement letters are blunt about scope, conflicts, and nonpayment because she has seen what vagueness costs a small practice. In writing she is formal and economical, prefers a qualified sentence to a confident one, and closes internal notes with a short list of who does what.

people.name: Heather Munoz
people.title: Partner
people.persona: Leads prosecution strategy and is the partner clients call when an examiner's rejection reads worse than it is. She writes long, family-by-family portfolio reviews with numbered recommendations and a candid note on which continuations are worth the fees. Relaxed and quick in internal meetings, she becomes exacting on anything with her signature on it, and she will strike an unhedged conclusion from an associate's draft without comment.

people.name: Amanda Schwartz
people.title: Associate
people.persona: A methodical associate who drafts office action responses with the examiner's own language quoted back and answered point by point. She keeps a running issues list for each matter and tends to open client emails with the docket number and the single decision she needs. Her prose is careful and slightly over-cited, the habit of someone who expects a partner to check every reference.

people.name: Kelly Snyder
people.title: Associate
people.persona: Works mostly on the hardware startup matters and has a feel for founders who want the answer before the analysis. Her client updates are short and plain, with the caveats kept in a separate paragraph so they cannot be skimmed past. Internally she is the associate most likely to flag that a proposed filing strategy outruns a client's budget.

people.name: Sharon Woods
people.title: Docketing Manager
people.persona: Owns the docket and treats it as the firm's one unforgivable risk. She sends reminder notices in a fixed format, escalates without apology when an attorney has not confirmed a response date, and keeps her own reconciliation against the patent office records. Her writing is terse, procedural, and impossible to misread, and attorneys learn quickly that her deadlines are not suggestions.

people.name: Joseph Walker
people.title: Associate
people.persona: An associate who gravitates toward the freedom-to-operate and validity work, where he is comfortable living inside qualified conclusions. His memoranda carry the privilege legend at the top, define their scope before saying anything else, and separate what the record shows from what remains uncertain. He writes in long, balanced sentences and is slow to commit to a bottom line without a partner's review.

people.name: Richard Henderson
people.title: Patent Agent
people.persona: A patent agent with an engineer's instinct for mechanical and medical device claims, happiest working through drawings and prior art side by side. He drafts specifications that anticipate the obvious design-around and writes examiner interview summaries that are almost stenographic. In internal correspondence he is dry, concise, and inclined to answer a question with the relevant paragraph number.

people.name: Ashley Williams
people.title: Patent Agent
people.persona: Handles much of the university licensing office's prosecution and is practiced at translating inventor disclosures into claim language a licensee can value. She is patient with academic inventors and firm with their timelines, and her notes to them are courteous but leave no room to miss a response date. Her technical writing is orderly, with headings that track the claim structure.

people.name: Matthew Parrish
people.title: Patent Agent
people.persona: The agent most often assigned to prior art searches and to the first pass at portfolio landscape tables. He works quickly, writes in clipped bullet points, and is candid in internal notes about where a search may have gaps. He leaves the client-facing polish to the attorneys and says so.

people.name: David Chang
people.title: Patent Agent
people.persona: Focuses on electrical and embedded-systems inventions for the venture-backed hardware clients and is the one colleagues ask when a claim turns on how firmware actually behaves. He drafts tightly and prefers to resolve ambiguity with an examiner by phone before committing it to a written response. His emails are brief, technically exact, and careful never to state a legal conclusion that belongs to counsel.

timeline.summary: Firm moved into its current office.
